newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: Ok Tedi sees copper concentrate shipment in week.
newsitem.headline: Ok Tedi sees copper concentrate shipment in week.

text.p: An export shipment of Ok Tedi copper concentrates could leave Papua New Guinea within a week if the water levels hold in the Fly River and concentrate barge movements run according to plan, Ok Tedi Mining Ltd (OTML) said on Friday.
Barges are expected to begin delivering concentrate to the transhipment vessel, the Karabi, this weekend following the resumption of barge movements, OTML said.
Rainfall that began on Friday, June 27, enabled barges to move copper concentrate downriver toward the Karabi, moored in Port Moresby Harbour, the company said.
OTML said the Ok Tedi mine, in PNG's remote Western Province, and mill have resumed production.
OTML was forced to suspend barge traffic down the Fly from the port of Kiunga to the Karabi on June 2 due to low water levels in the Fly caused by drought.
In Friday's statement, OTML noted that June rainfall totalled about 162 mm, which was 280 mm down on the previous driest month for June since 1970.
It did not name the destination of the first shipment.
Concentrates from Ok Tedi are sold mostly to smelters in Asia and Europe.

Ok Tedi has long-term supply contracts with Germany's Norddeutsche Affinerie, Finland's Outokumpu Oy, Philippines Associated Smelting and Refining Corp (PASAR), South Korea's LG Metals Corp, Mitsui & Co Ltd and the Japanese Smelter Pool which consists of seven Japanese smelters.
The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd owns 52.6 percent of OTML and operates the mine.
The other partners are Canada's Inmet Mining Corp with 17.4 percent and the PNG government, which holds the rest.
